chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, (from al-Hasan), from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Amr ibn Sa‘id ibn Hilal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah, blessings of Allah upon him: 'Guide me.' He said: 'I advise you with the mindfulness of Allah, and piety, and diligent effort, and know that no effort benefits which has no piety in it, and look at those who are below you, and do not look at those who are above you,

for how often has Allah, Most High, said to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family: 'So do not be deluded by their wealth and their children,' and He said: 'And do not extend your eyes to what We have given pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world.'

And if your soul drives you toward anything of that, then know that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant peace, had barley for his sustenance, and his sweet was dates when he found them, and his fuel was palm branches,

and when you are afflicted by a calamity, then remember your affliction by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, for indeed the people will never be afflicted with the like of it ever.

key_terms.اجْتِهَاد: ijtihad — diligent effort and striving in worship
key_terms.السَّعَف: sa‘af — dried palm branches used as fuel
key_terms.تَقْوَى: taqwa — God-consciousness; mindfulness of one’s duties to Allah
key_terms.وَرَع: wara‘ — piety; abstaining from what is forbidden and doubtful

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam al-Sadiq give about taqwa, piety, and worldly attachment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) advises Amr ibn Sa‘id ibn Hilal on the foundations of spiritual life: mindfulness of Allah (taqwa), piety (wara‘), and diligent effort. He warns that effort without piety is fruitless, and counsels always looking at those less fortunate rather than those more fortunate. He cites two Quranic verses (9:55, 20:131) warning against being dazzled by worldly wealth, and reminds him that the Prophet (s) lived with the simplest provisions—barley for food, dates for sweets, and palm branches for fuel. He concludes that when calamity strikes, one should remember the greatest loss: the passing of the Prophet (s).
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 25. And with the first chain of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, (from al-Hassan), from ‘Ali ibn Uqba, from Abi Kahmas, from Amru ibn Saeed ibn Hilal, who said:

I requested Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: ’Guide me.’ He said: ’My admonition to you is to be mindful of your duties to Allah (taqwa), to refrain from that which is forbidden and to make a strenuous effort (to win His Pleasure). And you should know that any effort, which is not coupled with abstaining from that, which is forbidden, has no benefit. And always look at those who are lower than you, and do not look at those who are above you.

For how often has Allah, Most High, advised His messenger: ’So do not be deluded by their wealth and their children’, (al-Tawbah, 9:55), and again He said: ’And do not even look at the wordly wealth. We have let some pairs of disbelievers to gain, it is only an allurement of the life of this world....’ (Taha, 20:131)."

And if your passion (or desires) drive you towards any of those things, then you should be aware that the Prophet, peace be upon him, and his progeny, had barley for daily subsistence, dates for his sweet dish, when available, and the source of warmth (firewood, fuel) was from the branches of the palm tree.
And when any calamity befalls you, then remember how you were tested by the passing away of the Prophet, peace be upon him; for the people will never face a similar tribulation ever again."
